title: Lekishi chapter manifest
description: historical/chapters/<id>.yaml: what a chapter is called, the window it opens on, its story, or its stories, as ordered lists of event and relationship ids, and the owner's approval. The approval pins a digest of the manifest and every record and source it reaches; `pnpm approvals` shows what changed since the last approval and prints the digest. The owner writes the approval; no one else does.

story.description: The chapter's story, when it has one. A chapter with several writes `stories` instead.

steps.description: The story in presentation order, which is not a claim that one step preceded or caused another. Each step is an event or relationship id with its caption: `- akimeya-landfall-753: The landfall at 秋妻屋浦`.

stories.description: A chapter's stories, when it has more than one (rfd/0002/CHAPTER_STORIES.adoc). The first is the story the chapter opens on. Each is published as its own story record, `lks:story:<key>`, and one approval covers them all.

key.description: The story's id, `lks:story:<key>`, unique across the project. A chapter that had one story keeps its chapter id as the first story's key, so nothing published under it moves.

title.description: The story's name in the chapter's story switcher, shorter than its summary.

window.description: The window the story opens on, by default its `span`. The first story opens on the chapter's `window` and does not write one. A step wholly outside a story's window is a coda step, and its caption starts "Coda — ".

include.description: Records the chapter publishes that its story does not step through, such as a relationship the map draws as an arc.
